text.intro:
The Ashfold Knitting Circle meets weekly and has not agreed on anything since 1998.
Five knitters are involved. Determine each knitter's day, project, yarn and setback.
- **Knitter**: Maudie, Lionel, Serafina, Ebba and Nkechi.
- **Day** (listed from earlier to later): Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
- **Project**: a cable-knit blanket, a shawl of impossible lace, a pair of argyle socks, a dog coat and a tea cosy shaped like a hen.
- **Yarn**: hand-spun alpaca, mill-end acrylic, nettle fibre, recycled sari silk and undyed Shetland.
- **Setback**: a dropped stitch in row nine, a cat, losing the pattern entirely, a misread chart and running out of dye lot.
Every knitter has a different day, project, yarn and setback, so within each category every item is used exactly once.
clues: The knitter who works in recycled sari silk falls somewhere between Monday and Nkechi in day order.

At least one of the following holds, and possibly more than one: (a) The knitter who is making a pair of argyle socks and the knitter who is set back by a dropped stitch in row nine are exactly one day apart in day order, in one direction or the other. (b) One of Tuesday and the knitter who is making a dog coat sits at an odd-numbered day and the other at an even-numbered day.
The knitter who is making a cable-knit blanket falls somewhere between Thursday and Ebba in day order.

The following two do NOT both hold; either one alone may hold, and so may neither: (a) The knitter who is set back by a dropped stitch in row nine and Thursday are exactly one day apart in day order, in one direction or the other. (b) The knitter who is making a cable-knit blanket is exactly one day earlier than the knitter who is set back by running out of dye lot, with no day in between.
Nkechi is earlier than Thursday in day order. Nkechi and the knitter who works in hand-spun alpaca are exactly one day apart in day order, in one direction or the other.
Friday and the knitter who is making a pair of argyle socks both sit at odd-numbered days or both at even-numbered days.
The knitter who is set back by a misread chart and the knitter who works in undyed Shetland are exactly two days apart in day order.
The knitter who is making a pair of argyle socks is not set back by a cat. Lionel is earlier than the knitter who is set back by a cat in day order.
Lionel and the knitter who works in nettle fibre are exactly four days apart in day order.
The knitter who is set back by running out of dye lot is exactly one day earlier than Serafina, with no day in between.

At least one of the following holds, and possibly more than one: (a) Lionel is earlier than the knitter who works in undyed Shetland in day order. (b) Nkechi is earlier than the knitter who is making a pair of argyle socks in day order.
The knitter who is making a tea cosy shaped like a hen is earlier than the knitter who works in mill-end acrylic in day order.
